sections.title: Furniture Industry Backdrop — Western US Perspective
sections.content: Returned datasets are national US-level only; no state-by-state western breakdown was supplied. The synthesis below applies US macro indicators that disproportionately affect western state furniture markets — where elevated home values, household formation, and renovation exposure run hotter than the national mean. Furnishings spending has compounded steadily (2022 → 2025: $476.1B → $507.3B), while consumer sentiment, real disposable income, and single-family housing starts have deteriorated sharply in early 2026. For western retailers, the conflicting signals — softening demand indicators versus enduring renovation spend in building materials — define the strategy window heading into H2 2026.

sections.title: Furnishings Spending vs Total Durable Goods Purchase
Housing & Real Estate Indicators (Relevance to Furniture Demand)
Strategic Insights for Western US Furniture Retailers

data.title: Furnishings spend outpaces broader durable goods modestly
data.evidence: Furnishings & HH equipment PCE rose from $476.1B (2022) to $507.3B (2025), a +6.6% cumulative gain. Total durable goods grew faster (+9.0%) but pulled by autos — furnishings gaining share within household segment of demand.

data.title: Housing starts contraction poses replacement-cycle risk
data.evidence: May 2026 housing starts dropped to 1,177K from a Q1 average near 1,418K — a ~17% decline in 4 months. Western markets (CA, WA, OR, AZ) typically lead this cycle and signal fewer new-home furniture furnish opportunities in late 2026.

data.title: Real income erosion dampens discretionary ticket size
data.evidence: Real disposable personal income fell from $18,135 (Jan 2026) to $17,984 (May 2026) — 5-month decline of 0.83%. Combined with sentiment falling 27.4% from July 2025, furniture trade-down risk is elevated.

data.title: Building materials momentum signals renovation tailwind
data.evidence: Building materials retail sales climbed steadily from $586.3B (Jun 2025) to $623.4B (May 2026), +6.3% in 12 months. Western household renovation exposure is among the highest nationally given elevated median home values ($332,700 in 2024, +18% vs 2022).

data.title: Inflation + savings attrition compresses net furniture demand
data.evidence: CPI +4.2% YoY to 333.98 means furniture unit volumes must rise faster than spend to grow. Personal savings rate fell from 5.4% (2024) to 4.6% (2025), indicating households have less buffer for future purchases — favouring essentials and lower-ticket SKUs.
